entries.name: startswith_byte_constant_long_arg-errored#0
entries.script: [S1] `Coll[Byte](1,2,3)` CONSTANT (specialised `$mcB$sp`) `.startsWith(ys)` where `ys` is declared `Coll[Byte]` but evaluates to a `Coll[Long]` — the lie carried by an `If` whose branches disagree, so no static check can reject it. `CollOverArray.startsWith` (`:44`) is `toArray.startsWith(ys.toArray)`, and in specialised code that casts the ARGUMENT's array to `[B`: `ClassCastException`. **SEPARATING, and the second separating family after getOrElse** — here it is the argument's array that is cast, not an item.

entries.name: startswith_byte_concrete_long_arg-accept#1
entries.script: [S2] The GENERIC twin with the SAME argument RETURNS **`true`** at cost 90 — because Scala's `Array.startsWith` compares boxed elements and `java.lang.Long(1) == java.lang.Byte(1)` numerically. **THE WORST ROW IN THE FAMILY and the one to lead with:** the JVM does not merely accept the ill-typed argument, it answers TRUE. An implementation holding one representation cannot produce both this and S1.

entries.name: startswith_bool_constant_long_arg-errored#2
entries.script: [S3] The same on the `$mcZ$sp` kind: a `Coll[Boolean]` CONSTANT with a `Coll[Long]` argument throws. **SEPARATING.**

entries.name: startswith_bool_concrete_long_arg-accept#3
entries.script: [S4] Its generic twin returns **`false`** at cost 90 — the boxed comparison runs and simply fails (a Boolean is not numerically equal to 1L). Together with S2 this says the generic answer is the ITEMS' answer, not a refusal.

entries.name: startswith_indices_long_arg-errored#4
entries.script: [S5] The same on the `$mcI$sp` kind (`indices`): throws. **SEPARATING.**

entries.name: startswith_int_concrete_long_arg-accept#5
entries.script: [S6] Its generic twin returns `false` at cost 90 (`0` is not `1L`).

entries.name: startswith_byte_constant_empty_long_arg-errored#6
entries.script: [S7] A ZERO-LENGTH ill-typed argument still throws on the specialised receiver: the array cast precedes any length check. **SEPARATING, and the sharpest of the set** — there is no element to compare, so an implementation can only reproduce it by modelling the cast.

entries.name: startswith_byte_concrete_empty_long_arg-accept#7
entries.script: [S8] Its generic twin returns `true` at cost 85 — vacuously, every collection starts with an empty one.

entries.name: startswith_byte_constant_wellformed-accept#8
entries.script: [S9] **CONTROL:** the specialised receiver with a well-typed `Coll[Byte](1)` argument returns `true` at cost 45. S1 is not about startsWith being unavailable.

entries.name: startswith_byte_concrete_wellformed-accept#9
entries.script: [S10] **CONTROL:** the generic receiver, same argument, `true` at cost 75.

entries.name: endswith_byte_constant_long_arg-errored#10
entries.script: [E1] `endsWith` (`:46`) is the same shape as `startsWith` and throws on the specialised receiver. **SEPARATING.**

entries.name: endswith_byte_concrete_long_arg-accept#11
entries.script: [E2] Its generic twin returns **`false`** at cost 90 — with the SAME argument that made S2 `true`. The asymmetry is the data, not the types: `(1,2,3)` starts with `1L` and does not end with it. A row that pins the comparison as numeric rather than refused.

entries.name: endswith_byte_constant_wellformed-accept#12
entries.script: [E3] **CONTROL:** the specialised receiver with `Coll[Byte](3)` returns `true` at cost 45.
